sentences.text: these writ petitions are disposed of by this common judgment.

2. The petitioners in these writ petitions were the successful bidders in the tender floated by the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) for allotting of spaces within its bus station in Palakkad.

Consequently, the petitioners erected temporary sheds within the above property on the Manoj R vs Palakkad Municipality on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188217403/
4 strength of the No-objection certificate issued by the KSRTC.
They had executed agreements and deposited the requisite amount with the KSRTC.

Although the petitioners have submitted applications before the 2 nd respondent, to assign temporary building numbers for their WP(C)
Nos.24796, 24658 & 29545 of 2023 2025:KER:50276 sheds, to enable them to apply for license, the applications have not been considered.
Subsequently, they have also submitted representations to the 2nd respondent, to assign the temporary numbers.
But, the representations have also not been considered till date.
In W.P.(C) No. 20664 of 2023, a case of an identical nature, this Court had directed the 2nd respondent to consider applications for temporary building numbers.
The petitioners are entitled to the benefit of the said judgment.

Hence, the writ petitions 3. Heard; the learned counsel for the petitioners, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the 1st respondent - Municipality and the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the KSRTC.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that, the petitioners would be satisfied if the 2 nd respondent consider their applications for temporary building numbers.

The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the KSRTC submits that, the petitioners have already instituted civil suits before the jurisdictional Court and orders of temporary injunction have been passed against the KSRTC from evicting the petitioners from the property.

Moreover, alleging that the temporary sheds have been unauthorisedly constructed in the property,
the 2 nd respondent has refused to issue occupancy certificate to the KSRTC for their building.

On a consideration of the facts and the materials on record, especially that petitioners' request for temporary building number for their sheds is pending consideration before the 2nd respondent and that orders of temporary injunction have been passed against the KSRTC, without expressing anything on the merits of the matter, I dispose of these writ petitions, by directing the 2 nd respondent to consider the representations submitted by the petitioners, WP(C) Nos.24796, 24658 & 29545 of 2023 2025:KER:50276 in accordance with law and as expeditiously as possible, at any rate, within 60 days from the date of production of a copy of the judgment, after affording the petitioners and the authorised representative of the KSRTC an opportunity of being heard.
It would be up to the petitioner in W.P.(C) No.24658 of 2023 a copy of the pleadings in the writ petition before the 2nd respondent along with a copy of the judgment.
The writ petition is ordered accordingly.

Sd/-
C.S.DIAS, JUDGE SCB.08.07.25.

4 strength of the No-objection certificate issued by the KSRTC.
They had executed agreements and deposited the requisite amount with the KSRTC.
The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the KSRTC submits that, the petitioners have already instituted civil suits before the jurisdictional Court and orders of temporary injunction have been passed against the KSRTC from evicting the petitioners from the property.
Moreover, alleging that the temporary sheds have been unauthorisedly constructed in the property,
the 2 nd respondent has refused to issue occupancy certificate to the KSRTC for their building.
opennyai_summary.decision:
On a consideration of the facts and the materials on record, especially that petitioners' request for temporary building number for their sheds is pending consideration before the 2nd respondent and that orders of temporary injunction have been passed against the KSRTC, without expressing anything on the merits of the matter, I dispose of these writ petitions, by directing the 2 nd respondent to consider the representations submitted by the petitioners, WP(C) Nos.24796, 24658 & 29545 of 2023 2025:KER:50276 in accordance with law and as expeditiously as possible, at any rate, within 60 days from the date of production of a copy of the judgment, after affording the petitioners and the authorised representative of the KSRTC an opportunity of being heard.
The writ petition is ordered accordingly.
